source_span: While US 10-year nominal yields are up around 97bps so far this year, only around 10bps of that is due to higher breakevens. The remainder reflects significantly higher real yields, which are now at levels last seen in 2008.
source_chain: Strong flash PMIs (58.4 vs 55.3, a 5-year high) trigger the worst Treasury selloff since April 2025, therefore decomposing the ~97bps YTD rise in the 10yr shows only ~10bps comes from breakevens (stable 3+ years) and term premium is flat (18 months, so not fiscal fear), therefore the move must be about policy rates and a higher neutral rate driven by growth strength/AI capex/geopolitics (Warsh) with Raskin's neutral-rate estimate elevated but still inside a plausible range, now edging toward its upper bound — invalidation: breakevens starting to move, or yields pushing through the top of that plausible neutral-rate range, would flip the story from growth-repricing to inflation- or term-premium-driven.
pulse_chain: Flash composite PMI beats sharply (58.4 vs 55.3, a five-year high) causing the worst Treasury session since April 2025, therefore per Deutsche Bank only ~10bps of the ~97bps YTD yield rise is breakevens (barely moved in 3+ years) and term premium has been flat for 18 months (ruling out fiscal fear), therefore what's left is the Fed/policy-rate path — hike odds rising to 71% and Goldman adding a second October hike — with DB's Raskin flagging yields edging toward the top of his plausible neutral-rate range, and banks split on when this becomes an equity problem (JPM's 5.5% fair value vs MS's 4.50% trigger vs GS's speed threshold vs BTIG's 4.92% floor).
why: The pulse reproduces DB's specific decomposition (~10bps breakevens vs the rest real yield, term premium flat for 18 months ruling out fiscal fear) attributed to the correct bank, and its 'what's left is the Fed' step matches DB's own 'must therefore largely be about policy rates and a higher neutral rate,' with the hike-odds evidence corroborated by the same day's companion DB note (Early Morning Reid) rather than invented.
